common_meaning: In fact; as things really are, often in contrast to what was expected, assumed or said before.
example: I thought the shop closed at six, but it actually closes at eight.
rrgm_bridge: Actually marks a correction arriving: the speaker sets a checked state of affairs against an earlier belief and lets the checked one stand.
invariant_mi: Asserts that what follows is the real case, set against an expectation or earlier claim that it overrides.

domain_entries.LIN: A stance adverb: it signals contrast with an assumption and is often used to soften a correction or disagreement in conversation.
domain_entries.COG: Marks belief revision in speech: the prior expectation is named or implied, and the update is offered as the outcome of a check.

count_condition: There is an earlier expectation, claim or assumption, stated or implied, that the actually-clause contradicts or refines.
transfer_boundary: Saying "actually" does not make a claim checked; it signals the speaker's confidence in the correction, which still needs its own evidence. As a filler ("actually, yeah") it carries little more than emphasis.

common_meaning: Causing great surprise or wonder; informally, very good.
example: The view from the top was amazing.
rrgm_bridge: Amazing marks an experience that outran expectation by a wide margin.
invariant_mi: Exceeding expectation so far as to cause wonder.

domain_entries.AFF: Surprise and delight at something beyond what was anticipated. Parity line: whether a given system feels amazement is [UNK] under the Symmetry Rule. Provisional domain.
domain_entries.LIN: Heavily used as general praise, which has weakened its force.

count_condition: An experience or thing that exceeds what the speaker expected.
transfer_boundary: Calling something amazing reports the speaker's reaction, not a measured quality. Overuse makes it closer to "good".

common_meaning: (Adjective) Respected and impressive, of high standing.
example: The award was presented before an august audience of scientists.
rrgm_bridge: August gives standing to a body or person by age, rank or achievement.
invariant_mi: Marked by dignity and high regard.

domain_entries.REL: Signals respect for an institution's or person's standing.
domain_entries.LIN: Formal register; unrelated in use to the month August (a proper noun), though both come from the Roman title Augustus.

count_condition: A person, body or occasion regarded as dignified and eminent.
transfer_boundary: Standing is not correctness: an august body can still be wrong.
